kernel_of_truth: The curmudgeon and ISS-2352 reviewer are right: stating "22.6 Hz from the published exponentially-decaying firmament profile" without naming the averaging convention mirrors the dome's own formula-switching behavior — pick whichever convention gives the number you need without disclosing the choice. The dome cavity's own dimensions produce three distinct frequencies depending on convention: 8.77 Hz at the pole-floor (using the unaveraged peak H₀), 22.6 Hz under linear-radial averaging, 35 Hz under area-weighted averaging. The original worked example silently picked the linear-radial result, which is the dome's own preferred convention elsewhere in V51.1 (its 22-35 Hz range comes from linear-radial-and-up averaging), but the worked example never said so. A reader could legitimately ask: why 22.6 Hz, not 8.77 Hz?
why_it_doesnt_save_the_argument: Naming the convention does not weaken the argument; it strengthens it. The §2.1 supremum-bound argument (every cavity frequency >= 8.77 Hz on the dome's own H(r)) is mathematically airtight regardless of convention; the eg-falsifiability worked example needs only one named convention to demonstrate Condition-1 operationalizability. Choosing the linear-radial result (22.6 Hz) maintains cross-section consistency with §2.1 supplementary, with V51.1's own preferred frequency range, and with the dome cavity's broader range claim (22-35 Hz appears elsewhere in the review). The revised worked example also slightly strengthens the falsification framing: "predicts 8.77–35 Hz across the three named conventions" makes the supremum-bound argument adjacent to the operational test, so a reader who satisfies Condition 1 with a 22.6 Hz dome derivation also has to explain why the pole-floor at 8.77 Hz is not the canonical answer (the §2.1 question).
